steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
**Transformers learn which parts of the input to pay attention to when processing each element.**

Key ideas:

- **Attention mechanism** — every token looks at every other token and asks "how relevant are you to me?" producing weighted relationships
- **No sequential processing** — unlike RNNs, all tokens are processed in parallel
- **Query/Key/Value** — each token creates a query (what am I looking for?), keys (what do I offer?), and values (what do I actually pass along?)
- **Multiple heads** — attention runs in parallel several times, capturing different types of relationships
- **Stack layers** — repeated attention + feedforward layers build increasingly abstract representations

The result: a model that captures long-range dependencies efficiently, which is why it scales so well.
